source_definition: Given a finite loopless subcubic plane graph, with parallel edges permitted and its full topological embedding fixed, output YES exactly when adding edges on the same vertex set can produce a three-vertex-connected cubic plane supergraph extending that embedding, and NO otherwise. The embedding includes disconnected-component nesting, face boundaries and the outer face. A finite rational polygonal drawing represents it; edges may bend.
target_definition: Given the same kind of fixed plane input, output YES exactly when some finite three-vertex-connected cubic plane supergraph extends its embedding, allowing both additional vertices and additional edges, and NO otherwise. Three-connectivity requires at least four vertices. The graph is a subgraph, not necessarily induced. All disconnected components and their nesting must be preserved. Rational polygonal edge arcs represent topological embeddings; straight-line geometry is not fixed.
required_result: Construct a deterministic polynomial-time map F from the edge-only fixed-embedding three-connected cubic augmentation decision problem to its variant allowing new vertices, preserving YES and NO. Boolean-answer recovery G is the identity. The requested conclusion is NP-hardness of the fixed-embedding target.
